experiences.name: Street Food Tour in Centro Histórico
experiences.description: Explore the bustling streets of Mexico City's historic center sampling iconic local dishes such as tacos al pastor, tlayudas, tamales, and churros from legendary street vendors and traditional market stalls like Mercado San Juan.

experiences.name: Visit the National Museum of Anthropology
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Mexico's rich pre-Hispanic heritage at one of the world's greatest museums, featuring the famous Aztec Sun Stone, Mayan artifacts, and exhibits spanning thousands of years of Mesoamerican civilization.

experiences.name: Xochimilco Trajinera Boat Ride and Local Food Experience
experiences.description: Float along the ancient Aztec canals of Xochimilco on a colorful trajinera boat, enjoying local snacks, fresh elotes, and quesadillas sold by vendors on passing boats while soaking in the vibrant festive atmosphere.

experiences.name: Cooking Class in Coyoacán
experiences.description: Join a hands-on traditional Mexican cooking class in the charming bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán, learning to prepare classic dishes like mole, chiles en nogada, and handmade tortillas using fresh local ingredients from nearby markets.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum and Neighborhood Walk
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Casa Azul, the birthplace and home of legendary artist Frida Kahlo, then stroll through the colorful cobblestone streets of Coyoacán exploring local artisan markets, colonial architecture, and authentic cantinas.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Travel from airport to hotel in Centro Histórico via Metro Line 5 to Pantitlán, then transfer to Line 2 toward Tasqueña, exiting at Zócalo station (budget-friendly ~$5 MXN per ride). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walking tour of the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), Mexico City's massive main square. Explore the exterior of the Catedral Metropolitana (free entry), stroll past the Palacio Nacional and admire Diego Rivera's famous murals inside (free admission). Walk along Madero Street, a pedestrian avenue lined with historic buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lit-up Zócalo at dusk — the square is magical after dark. Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site area (view the exterior for free at night) and enjoy the street atmosphere of Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the hotel — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan (15-min walk from hotel) — try a torta or quesadilla from market stalls for around 40–70 MXN (~$2–4 USD).
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (budget-friendly branch on Palma Street) or a local taquería near Zócalo — tacos de guisado for 15–25 MXN each. Total dinner budget: ~80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your luggage light on the Metro. Use the CDMX Metro app for navigation. Exchange currency at a casa de cambio near the airport or Centro for better rates than hotel exchange. Store valuables securely.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor Museum (entry ~$85 MXN, free on Sundays) — an incredible Aztec archaeological site right in Centro Histórico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and artifacts. Afterward, walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior (free to view from outside; interior galleries ~$85 MXN).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the historic Mercado de la Merced (10-min walk or short Metro ride) — one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America. Browse local produce, spices, street food, and everyday Mexican life. Then explore the charming streets of Barrio Chino (Chinatown) nearby for a unique cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Avenida Francisco I. Madero toward the Torre Latinoamericana. Take the elevator to the observation deck (~$100 MXN) for panoramic night views of the city. Return to hotel via a stroll through the illuminated Centro.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba (historic café near hotel) — chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla for ~80–120 MXN. A true CDMX cultural experience.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de la Merced — freshly made enchiladas, pozole, or a comida corrida (set lunch) for ~60–90 MXN.
meals.dinner: Taquería Los Cocuyos near Zócalo — famous late-night taquería, tacos de sesos or bistec for ~20 MXN each. A local institution.

day_by_day.notes: Sundays offer free museum entry — plan museum-heavy days accordingly. Wear comfortable shoes as today involves a lot of walking. Carry small bills for market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro Line 3 to Coyoacán (exit at Viveros or Coyoacán station) — about 40 minutes from Centro. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum 'La Casa Azul' (book tickets online in advance ~$270 MXN — worth it!). Explore the colorful colonial neighborhood with its cobblestone streets and vibrant murals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Jardín Hidalgo and Jardín Centenario — Coyoacán's twin plazas buzzing with artists, musicians, and locals. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for artisan crafts and street food. Browse the Leon Trotsky Museum nearby (~$80 MXN) for a fascinating slice of history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Walk through the Alameda Central park as the sun sets. Visit the Laboratorio Arte Alameda (contemporary art museum, ~$50 MXN) if time permits, or simply relax in the park and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Grab a torta or tamale from a street cart near the hotel before heading to Metro — ~30–50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas for ~60–100 MXN. Fresh aguas frescas ~20 MXN.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro — try Restaurante El Popular on 5 de Mayo Street, open 24 hours, beloved by locals. Soup and main course ~100–150 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least a week in advance online — they sell out fast. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. Avoid rush hour Metro (7–9am, 6–8pm) if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line 2 to Pino Suárez, then a bus or pesero (~10 MXN) to Xochimilco — visit the famous floating gardens (chinampas). Rent a trajinera (colorful boat) with other travelers to split costs (~$200–300 MXN per hour per boat, shareable). Enjoy the canals, mariachi boats, and local vendors selling food and crafts from their boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro and visit the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) on Tacuba Street (~$85 MXN, free on Sundays) — stunning collection of Mexican art from the 16th century to the 20th century in a gorgeous Neoclassical building. Spend 1–2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Join the evening paseo (evening stroll) culture in Centro. Head to Plaza Garibaldi (~20-min walk or short Metro ride) to watch mariachi bands perform — no entry fee, just tip the musicians. Soak in one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural traditions.

meals.breakfast: Mercado de San Juan — fresh fruit, juices, and a breakfast quesadilla or huevos rancheros for ~60–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: On the trajinera in Xochimilco — buy food directly from vendor boats (elotes, quesadillas, carnitas tacos) for ~50–100 MXN. Very festive experience.
meals.dinner: Near Plaza Garibaldi — try Salón Tenampa (historic pulquería and cantina) for a drink and light snack, or grab street tacos al pastor from nearby stands for ~20 MXN each.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best visited on weekends when it's most lively. Go in the morning to avoid crowds. Share a trajinera with other hostel travelers or tourists to reduce cost. Keep belongings secure at Plaza Garibaldi at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor one more time if missed, or head to the Archivo General de la Nación (free entry) to see its stunning murals. Then walk to the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (~15-min walk from Centro) — the best place for affordable authentic Mexican crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining!
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon stroll through Centro Histórico — revisit your favorite spots, grab a coffee at a local café, and explore any streets you missed. Visit the Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP) building on Argentina Street for free — Diego Rivera's monumental mural cycle covering 235 panels, completely free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Centro. Reflect on the trip at a rooftop bar or café with views of the Zócalo. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or visit a local panadería (bakery) for pan dulce and café de olla — ~30–50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a local family restaurant (fonda) near La Ciudadela — soup, main dish, agua fresca, and dessert for ~80–100 MXN. The best budget meal in Mexico City.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell meal — try El Hidalguense in Centro for barbacoa (lamb slow-cooked in maguey leaves), a weekend specialty ~150–200 MXN. Or return to a favorite taquería for one last round of tacos.

day_by_day.notes: La Ciudadela market is open daily and prices are generally fair — still worth negotiating politely. The SEP murals are one of Mexico City's most underrated free attractions. Keep Metro fare and airport transport budget in mind for departure day. Metro + bus to airport costs ~$20 MXN total vs. ~$300–500 MXN for a taxi.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approximately 40–60 minutes by taxi or Uber, ~$15–20 USD). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the stunning murals by Diego Rivera inside (free entry, open until 17:00). Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian boulevard lined with colonial architecture, shops, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the iconic Templo Mayor archaeological site neighborhood for a relaxed evening. Walk around the lit-up Zócalo at dusk — the atmosphere is magical. Explore the nearby streets of the historic center as they come alive at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba (Tacuba 28, Centro) — a Mexico City institution since 1912. Try enchiladas, chiles en nogada, or tamales in a beautiful colonial setting. Budget ~$10–15 USD per person.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Palma 23, Centro) — beloved local restaurant famous for traditional Mexican cuisine. Try the sopa de lima or mole negro with rice. Budget ~$15–20 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on the immediate surroundings of your hotel to ease into the city. Carry small bills in pesos for tips and street snacks. Exchange currency at a bank or ATM rather than the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with breakfast at a local market, then head to the Templo Mayor Museum (Seminario 8, Centro). This world-class archaeological museum sits on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the artifacts and the open-air ruins. Entry ~$4 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes (Fine Arts Palace) — a stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco building housing murals by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros. Browse the adjacent Alameda Central park. Then walk to the Museo Franz Mayer (folk art and decorative arts museum) nearby. Entry to each ~$3–5 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Dolores Street, just off Alameda Central, for an eclectic evening stroll. Then head to the rooftop bar at Hotel Downtown or a nearby cantina for drinks with views of the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Mercado de San Juan (Aranda 7, Centro) — a gourmet market with fresh juices, chilaquiles, and local cheeses. Budget ~$5–8 USD.
meals.lunch: Los Cocuyos (Bolívar 56, Centro) — a legendary taco stand famous for tacos de tripa, suadero, and cabeza. Authentic, cheap, and delicious. Budget ~$5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (Isabel la Católica 30, Centro) — elegant yet affordable Mexican cuisine in a beautiful courtyard setting. Try the mole negro or cochinita pibil. Budget ~$15–20 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Templo Mayor and Bellas Artes are within walking distance of each other and your hotel. Wear comfortable shoes — you'll be on your feet most of the day. Tuesday is free entry day at some national museums, check in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or metro to Coyoacán neighborhood (30–40 min from Centro). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul / Blue House) — Frida Kahlo's iconic home and studio. Book tickets online in advance as they sell out fast. Entry ~$10 USD. Spend 1.5 hours exploring the museum and garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets and colonial plazas. Visit the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, browse artisan craft markets, and pop into the Mercado de Coyoacán for street food. Optional: visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky (the exiled revolutionary's home). Entry ~$3 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Uber. Spend the evening exploring the lively nightlife scene around República de Uruguay and surrounding streets. Stop at a traditional pulquería (pulque bar) for a uniquely Mexican experience.

meals.breakfast: At your hotel or a nearby café in Centro before departing — try pan dulce (Mexican sweet bread) with café de olla (spiced coffee). Budget ~$4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga, enfrijoladas, or fresh ceviche. Authentic and budget-friendly. Budget ~$6–9 USD.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Durango 200, Roma Norte) — a celebrated seafood restaurant known for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Slightly upscale but worth it. Budget ~$20–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Coyoacán is best explored on foot once you arrive. The neighborhood is very safe and tourist-friendly. Metro Line 3 (Viveros station) is a budget-friendly option to get there (~$0.25 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber to Teotihuacán archaeological site (about 1 hour from Centro, ~$25–30 USD each way, or join a guided group tour for ~$30–40 USD including transport). Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Allow 3–4 hours on site. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city by early afternoon. Stop in the Tepito or La Lagunilla flea market area for a cultural browse (stay aware of your belongings). Alternatively, visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park — one of the finest archaeology museums in the world. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) at dusk, one of the largest urban parks in the world. Head to the Condesa or Roma neighborhood for a relaxed, trendy evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel or grab tamales and atole from a street vendor near the hotel before departing. Budget ~$3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: At Teotihuacán, eat at one of the restaurants near the site exit — try barbacoa (slow-cooked lamb) with handmade tortillas and salsa verde, a regional specialty. Budget ~$8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre (Álvaro Obregón 86, Roma Norte) — a beloved, no-frills spot celebrating corn-based Mexican cuisine. Creative, soulful dishes. Budget ~$12–18 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán is a full-morning excursion. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring plenty of water — the site is largely unshaded and can be hot even in March. Comfortable walking shoes are essential. If you prefer a guided experience, many Centro hotels can arrange half-day tours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica (flower market) for an immersive local market experience — a feast for the senses with flowers, produce, spices, and street food. Afterward, revisit any favorite spots in Centro Histórico or visit the Museo de la Ciudad de México (City Museum) for a deep dive into the city's history. Entry ~$2 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Xochimilco canals (about 1 hour from Centro by Uber, ~$15–20 USD). Rent a trajinera (colorful flat-bottomed boat) with a group and float through the ancient Aztec canal system. Mariachi boats and food vendors will float alongside you. A 2-hour boat ride costs ~$20–25 USD per boat (split with others). A truly unique Mexico City experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro for a final evening. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping on Madero Street or at Mercado de Artesanías. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a restaurant with a rooftop view of the Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: La Casa de las Enchiladas (near Centro) or a market breakfast at Mercado de la Merced — huevos rancheros, fresh fruit, and café de olla. Budget ~$5–8 USD.
meals.lunch: Street tacos and snacks from the vendors at Xochimilco canals — quesadillas, elotes (corn), and fresh fruit with chili and lime. Budget ~$6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Terraza del Centro (rooftop restaurant near Zócalo) or La Terraza de la Gran Hotel — enjoy your final Mexico City dinner with panoramic views of the illuminated historic center. Try cochinita pibil or chiles en nogada. Budget ~$18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best visited on weekends when it's lively and festive, but weekdays are quieter and more relaxed. Book trajinera boats directly at the embarcadero — no need to pre-book. This is a wonderful final-day experience that combines nature, history, and local culture. Pack any fragile souvenirs carefully for the journey home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the heart of Mexico City. Visit the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral (Catedral Metropolitana) and admire the exterior of the Palacio Nacional, home to Diego Rivera's iconic murals. Stroll through the historic streets of Centro Histórico, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with your expert local guide providing cultural and historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México overlooking the Zócalo, followed by a refined dinner at Azul Histórico, celebrated for its elevated regional Mexican cuisine in a breathtaking courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack and refreshments at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — upscale Mexican regional cuisine; try the chiles en nogada and artisanal mezcal pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light given the midday arrival. The Centro Histórico is very walkable from your hotel. Confirm your guided tour booking 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Templo Mayor Archaeological Site and its world-class museum. Explore the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán with a dedicated archaeologist guide who will bring the layers of history to life. Afterward, browse the artisan market at Plaza de Santo Domingo nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the finest anthropology museums in the world. Spend two to three hours with a private guide exploring pre-Columbian civilizations, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Follow with a leisurely walk through the lush Bosque de Chapultepec.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Pujol, consistently ranked among the best restaurants in the world. Chef Enrique Olvera's tasting menu is a masterpiece of contemporary Mexican cuisine. Book the omakase bar experience for the iconic Mole Madre, Mole Nuevo — a mole aged over 1,000 days.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a curated Mexican spread with chilaquiles, fresh tropical fruits, and café de olla
meals.lunch: Café del Museo inside the Museo Nacional de Antropología for a light gourmet lunch with a garden view
meals.dinner: Pujol — world-renowned tasting menu; reservations essential and should be made weeks in advance

day_by_day.notes: Pujol reservations are extremely competitive — book as early as possible, ideally 4–6 weeks ahead. Dress code at Pujol is smart casual to elegant. The Chapultepec area is about 20 minutes by private car from Centro Histórico.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient City of the Gods, approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Depart early to beat the crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon with your private archaeologist guide. Explore the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl with exclusive insight into the civilization that built them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at Teotihuacán with a visit to the Palace of Tepantitla to see the vibrant murals. Stop at a local artisan workshop on the return journey to see obsidian craftsmanship — a tradition dating back to the Aztec era. Optional: visit a local mezcal or pulque producer en route back to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and relax at the hotel spa or rooftop. Dinner at Contramar in Colonia Roma, the city's most iconic seafood restaurant, renowned for its tuna tostadas and red-and-green grilled fish. A beloved institution among Mexico City's culinary elite.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — packed gourmet picnic box can be arranged for the road
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your hotel or a curated bento from a local deli, enjoyed with views of the pyramids
meals.dinner: Contramar — legendary Mexico City seafood; try the tostadas de atún and pescado a la talla

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:30 AM to arrive at Teotihuacán before peak crowds and heat. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection — the site is expansive and exposed. The round trip with private driver is approximately 2.5 hours total travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private culinary experience: a premium cooking class and market tour at Mercado de San Juan, one of Mexico City's finest gourmet markets. Shop for rare chiles, heirloom corn, exotic cheeses, and fresh produce with a renowned local chef. Return to a private kitchen to prepare a multi-course traditional Mexican meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bohemian neighborhoods of Colonia Roma and Colonia Condesa on a private cultural walking tour. Discover Art Deco architecture, independent galleries, murals by emerging artists, and curated boutiques. Visit Casa Lamm cultural center for a rotating exhibition of contemporary Mexican art.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner mezcal tasting experience at a curated mezcalería in Colonia Roma, guided by a certified sommelier exploring terroir-driven expressions from Oaxaca, Guerrero, and Durango. Dinner at Quintonil, Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant focusing on native Mexican ingredients and modern technique — a must for food lovers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for a traditional Mexican spread with tamales, enfrijoladas, and fresh-squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your morning cooking class as a leisurely sit-down lunch
meals.dinner: Quintonil — contemporary Mexican haute cuisine; the tasting menu with wine pairing is highly recommended

day_by_day.notes: Quintonil reservations should also be made well in advance. The cooking class can be arranged through your hotel concierge or a premium culinary tour operator. Colonia Roma and Condesa are about 15 minutes by private car from Centro Histórico.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) in Coyoacán with a private guide — Frida Kahlo's iconic Blue House offers an intimate look into the life and art of Mexico's most celebrated painter. Afterward, explore the charming cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, one of the city's most picturesque and culturally rich neighborhoods. Browse the artisan market in the central plaza.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for a final exploration: visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and the Diego Rivera murals inside. Stop at the iconic Librería El Péndulo for a coffee and browse curated Mexican literature and design books as a cultural keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Rosetta, Chef Elena Reygadas' acclaimed restaurant set in a restored 19th-century mansion in Colonia Roma. The menu blends Italian sensibility with Mexican ingredients in an intimate, elegant atmosphere. End the evening with a digestif and live jazz at a nearby speakeasy-style bar in Colonia Juárez.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final indulgent spread; request a traditional Mexican hot chocolate and pan dulce
meals.lunch: El Hidalgense in Coyoacán — a beloved local institution for slow-cooked barbacoa and consommé, a true Mexico City tradition
meals.dinner: Rosetta — refined Mexican-Mediterranean cuisine; the pasta and seasonal tasting menu are exceptional

day_by_day.notes: Book La Casa Azul (Museo Frida Kahlo) tickets in advance as they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Coyoacán is approximately 30 minutes by private car from Centro Histórico. Consider arranging a late checkout with your hotel if your departure flight is in the evening.
